newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Repsol wins Venezuelan Mene Grande oil contract.
newsitem.headline: Repsol wins Venezuelan Mene Grande oil contract.

text.p: Spanish firm Repsol agreed Tuesday to pay $330 for the contract to operate Venezuela's Mene Grande oil field, state oil company Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA) said.
Seven other consortia bid for the field on the second day of Venezuela's third round of oil operating contract auctions. The second highest bidder was $187.6 million.
The field, discovered in 1914 on the south eastern shores of Lake Maracaibo in western Venezuela, currently produces 6,000 barrels per day (bpd) from 154 active wells.
The field has proven reserves of 100 million barrels, according to PDVSA estimates, with 444 other inactive wells.

Under the 20-year contract, the operator will produce hydrocarbons on behalf of PDVSA subsidiary Maraven in exchange for a fee worked out on a sliding scale. The operator must also invest at least $20 million within three years, although PDVSA expects investment to be higher.
The field was the last to be auctioned Tuesday.

Earlier the China National Petroleum Corporation (CNPC) agreed to pay $118 million to operate the Intercampo oil field; Argentina's Perez Companc, in association with the U.S.'s Williams Companies Inc then paid $153 million to operate the La Concepcion field.

Finally, U.S. company Pennzoil, in association with Saudi Arabian private company Nimir Petroleum Company Ltd and Venezuela's Ehcopek SA, paid $46 million for the contract to operate Venezuela's B2X.68/79 oil field
On Monday, total bids for five fields reserved for companies that had at least 30 percent Venezuelan participation reached $280 million.
A total of 131 companies are competing for 20 contracts to be sold this week with the winners determined purely by the size of their bids.
